question: Does the agreement make the Target liable (e.g., deem it a breach by the Target) for no-shop violations by its Representatives?
Fiduciary exception to the no-shop: what kind of third-party proposal permits the Target to engage (furnish information / negotiate)?
options: Superior Offer, or Acquisition Proposal reasonably likely/expected to result in a Superior Offer

question: Fiduciary exception to the no-shop: what fiduciary-duty standard must the board determine is met (regarding failure to engage)?
options: "Reasonably likely/expected to be inconsistent" with fiduciary duties
More likely than not violate fiduciary duties

question: Is a change of recommendation permitted on the basis of a board fiduciary determination alone (i.e., not tied to a Superior Offer or an Intervening Event)?
Change of recommendation in response to a Superior Offer: what fiduciary-duty standard must the board determine is met?
options: "Reasonably likely/expected to be inconsistent" with fiduciary duties
More likely than not violate fiduciary duties

question: Is a change of recommendation permitted in response to an Intervening Event?
Buyer's matching right before a change of recommendation: length of the initial matching (notice) period?
Buyer's matching right before a change of recommendation: length of the additional matching period after a material modification of the proposal?
Buyer's matching right before the Target terminates to accept a Superior Offer (fiduciary termination right): length of the initial matching period?
What breaches by the Target preclude it from exercising its fiduciary termination right? (select all that apply)
options: (Material) breach of other provisions of agreement
Breach of no-shop resulting in a Superior Offer
Material breach of no-shop resulting in a Superior Offer

question: Superior Offer definition: what percentage of the Target's stock must the proposal cover?
options: Greater than 50% but not "all or substantially all"
note: "50%" = the definition refers to 50% (e.g., "more than 50%" or "a majority"); "Greater than 50% but not all or substantially all" = e.g., 75% or 80%.

question: Superior Offer definition: is being more favorable "from a financial point of view" the sole stated basis for comparison (no other factors such as legal, regulatory, financing or timing aspects)?
Termination-fee tail provision: what must happen during the tail period with respect to the same or a different acquisition proposal for the tail fee to be payable? (select all that apply)
options: Different Acquisition Proposal - Must be approved or not opposed (or another similar action) during Tail Period (no closing requirement)
Different Acquisition Proposal - Must be approved or not opposed (or another similar action) during Tail Period and transaction must close after Tail Period
Different Acquisition Proposal - Must sign during Tail Period (no closing requirement)
Different Acquisition Proposal - Must sign during Tail Period and close after Tail Period
Different Acquisition Proposal must close during Tail Period
Same Acquisition Proposal - Must be approved or not opposed (or another similar action) during Tail Period and transaction must close after Tail Period
Same Acquisition Proposal - Must be approved or not opposed to (or another similar action) during Tail Period (no closing requirement)
Same Acquisition Proposal - Must close during Tail Period
Same Acquisition Proposal - Must sign during Tail Period (no closing requirement)
Same Acquisition Proposal - Must sign during Tail Period and close after Tail Period
note: Typically one "Same" and one "Different" option apply.

question: Termination-fee tail provision: must the acquisition proposal have been publicly disclosed/announced (for at least one of the termination triggers)?
Termination-fee tail provision: must the acquisition proposal not have been withdrawn (still pending) at the time of termination or of the stockholder meeting (for at least one trigger)?
Termination-fee tail provision: length of the tail period?
note: "within 12 months" = a period of 12 months (one year) after termination.

question: Ordinary-course covenant: is the Buyer's consent to deviate from the ordinary course a flat consent or one that may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed?
options: Consent may not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed

question: Ordinary-course covenant: does it require operation in the ordinary course "consistent with past practice"?
Ordinary-course covenant: what efforts standard qualifies the Target's obligation to operate in the ordinary course?
Negative interim operating covenants: does the "not unreasonably withheld" consent standard apply to all of the negative covenants or only to specified ones?
options: Applies only to specified negative covenants

question: Ordinary-course covenant: does it include an exception for actions taken in response to the pandemic (e.g., COVID-19 measures)?
Negative interim operating covenants: do they include an exception for actions taken in response to the pandemic (e.g., COVID-19 measures)?
